# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.
data.title: Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts (blocked by ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E)

# Intake Brief — Session isolation per child when implementing an epic

**Work item:** SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52 — "When implementing an epic start a new session for each child"
**Priority:** high | **Type:** epic

## Problem statement

When implementing an epic, all children are currently implemented within a single LLM session. Each child inherits the accumulated context of all previous children, diluting focus and risking context contamination between unrelated tasks.

## Users

- **AI agents** — multi-child epic implementations that currently run serially in one session.
- **Producers/operators** — agents that dispatch work via `/skill:implement` on parent items.

Example user story: "As an AI agent implementing epic SA-XXXX, when I invoke `/skill:implement SA-XXXX`, each child should be implemented in its own LLM session, giving it a clean context window focused solely on that child's ACs."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New session per child.** When implementing an epic, a new LLM session is started for each child item — each child receives a clean context window containing only that child's work-item description, ACs, and relevant context.
2. **Serial execution preserved.** Children are still implemented in dependency order (blocking items first), but each in its own session — the serial ordering remains intact.
3. **Session logging.** Each new session comments on the child work-item with its session ID: `<agent_action> - Session ID: <pi_session_id> - <path_to_sessions_log>` (per existing AGENTS.md convention).
4. **Parent still advanced last.** The parent item is only advanced to `in_review` after all children (across all sessions) have reached terminal status.
5. **Error isolation.** A failure in one child's session does not affect subsequent children's sessions; the parent phase reports which children failed and which succeeded.

## Constraints

- This is a procedural/organizational change — no code changes to the implement skill itself (which already handles parent recursion).
- The change applies to both AI agents and human operators following the workflow.
- Session boundaries must be explicit: each child's session starts with a fresh context, re-loading the work-item description and ACs.
- Worktree isolation per child is already in place and must be preserved.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 (Parent recursion): children are implemented serially within the same session ("Then implement that child by recursing into this procedure... and re-run `implement.py parent <parent-id>` for the next child").
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` workflow step 8: "End session — inform operator, summarize remaining tasks, clean up worktrees." — currently applied once at the end of the entire epic, not per child.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` step 58: session logging convention exists but is applied per work-item on new Pi session start, not per-child.

## Desired change

Update the procedural guidance in `AGENTS.md` (both global and project-level) to specify:

1. When `/skill:implement <parent-id>` is invoked and the item has children, a **new Pi session should be started for each child**.
2. Each child's session begins with the child work-item's description, ACs, and context loaded fresh.
3. After completing a child, the session ends (per existing convention), worktrees are cleaned up, and the next child starts a new session.
4. The parent is only considered complete after all child sessions have finished.

## Key files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` — global agent guidance; add session-per-child procedural step
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` — project-level agent guidance; mirror the global change
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 — clarify that each child recursion implies a new session (documentation alignment)

## Related work

- SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T: "implement skill: /skill:implement <parent-id> must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain" — the parent recursion mechanism that this epic builds on.
- SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR: "Reduce initial LLM context from skills and skill-related startup files" — related to context management but different scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — operational overhead:** starting new sessions per child means more session management. Mitigation: this is already the pattern for independent tasks; the overhead is minimal (session startup is fast).
- **Risk — context fragmentation:** each session must re-load relevant context for the child. Mitigation: the implement skill already loads the work-item description at session start.
- **Assumption:** "session" = Pi conversation session (with its own LLM context window); not a separate process or script.
- **Assumption:** serial execution is intentional and performance is not the primary concern; correctness and context isolation are.
- **Risk — scope creep:** this could evolve into a feature request for the implement skill itself to manage sessions. Mitigation: keep this epic scoped to procedural documentation; session orchestration is a separate concern.

# Implement skill: run risk/effort evaluation rather than failing on the gate for plan_complete items missing risk/effort

Companion to ContextHub P4 (WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7, RCA WL-0MTTS9FY00055QJV) — related-to: WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7 (cross-repo companion, see ContextHub worklog). This is a SorraAgents-tracked work item (skill source lives in `skill/implement/` of this repo, symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement`).

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher gates implement dispatch on `open/plan_complete` items having `risk ≤ Medium` and `effort ≤ Medium` (`classifyItemForDispatch` fails closed when risk/effort are absent). Items created without estimates are therefore **never implement-dispatchable** and no mechanism evaluates them (evidence: open_source_llm has 6 of 7 open plan_complete items with empty risk/effort — OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA et al.). The ContextHub dispatcher-side fix (P4) will either dispatch a risk/effort evaluation or adopt a default; either way the **implement skill** must behave correctly when invoked on (or alongside) an item whose estimates are missing — currently the effort/risk gate blocks the run instead of producing the missing data.

## Desired change

In the implement skill (`skill/implement/SKILL.md` and its scripts):
1. When starting implementation of a plan_complete item that lacks risk and/or effort, run the risk/effort evaluation (the effort-and-risk skill — `skill/effort-and-risk`/`effort_and_risk_skill`) **before/at gate time** and persist the estimates on the work item (wl update --risk/--effort), so the item is properly sized and the run proceeds — rather than failing on the gate.
2. Alternatively/additionally: when the dispatcher has already dispatched a standalone risk/effort evaluation for such an item, the implement skill accepts the item once estimates are present (no gate error).
3. Keep the gate for items WITH estimates (no behaviour change there); document the missing-estimate path in the SKILL.md and AGENTS guidance.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Invoking implement on a plan_complete item with empty risk/effort produces and persists risk/effort estimates and proceeds (or cleanly hands off to the evaluation), instead of refusing on the gate.
2. Estimates persist via `wl update` and the item becomes implement-dispatchable by the ContextHub dispatcher afterwards (cross-project fixture/step verified with OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA shape).
3. SKILL.md documents the missing-estimate flow; no regression for items with estimates.
4. Full project suite green (this repo).

## Key files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (+ `skill/implement/scripts/*`)
- `skill/effort-and-risk` (existing evaluation skill to reuse)

## Related

- ContextHub RCA WL-0MTTS9FY00055QJV and its P4 child (dispatcher-side); open_source_llm items OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA, OSL-0MST3DPNF00812I3, OSL-0MSG7Y9TI000KDUO, OSL-0MSG7YB8U004C1RE, OSL-0MSG7YE3S0021DZT, OSL-0MSG7YFZG007IH3D (evidence)

## Summary

`StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` / `ensure_claimed()` in
`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` compare the item's current status against
the string `"in_progress"`, but the `wl` CLI stores and returns statuses in
hyphenated form (`"in-progress"`). Consequently:

- `require_claimed()` **always raises `ClaimError`** for genuinely claimed
  items (observed while running `/skill:plan SA-0MTYJ5VFI003PZMI`: item
  status `"in-progress"` failed the `!= "in_progress"` guard). The
  SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9 fail-closed guard is therefore non-functional in
  production.
- `ensure_claimed()` never recognises an existing claim, so it performs a
  redundant `wl update --status in_progress` write on every call instead of
  being a read-only no-op.

Root cause check: `wl` (ContextHub `dist/commands/update.js`) explicitly
normalises underscore → hyphen on write ("stored statuses are (underscore →
hyphen) so `in_progress` matches the stored `in-progress`"), and the same
package's `show` returns `"in-progress"` in JSON. The unit tests in
`test_status_lifecycle.py` mock `wl show` responses with `status="in_progress"`
(underscore), so they never exercise the real CLI's hyphenated value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `require_claimed()` passes when the stored status is `"in-progress"` (hyphen) and fails closed only when it is genuinely not claimed.
- [ ] `ensure_claimed()` is a read-only no-op when the stored status is already `"in-progress"` (no `wl update` write).
- [ ] Unit tests assert behaviour against the hyphenated stored value (matching `wl show` output), in addition to any underscore variants.
- [ ] Full test suite passes.

Discovered-from: SA-0MTYJ5VFI003PZMI
data.title: StatusLifecycle.require_claimed/ensure_claimed compare against "in_progress" but wl stores "in-progress" — guard always fails closed

# Intake Brief: RCA — audit Phase 1 / Phase 2 Reliability

**Work Item:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL

## Headline Summary

Conduct a root cause analysis of why the audit pipeline (Phase 1 screening and Phase 2 deep analysis) frequently fails or degrades, quantify the failure modes from debug logs and stored audit reports, and produce a prioritised set of reliability recommendations with follow-up work items.

## Problem Statement

Audits routinely report `Ready to close: No` for *infrastructure* reasons rather than genuine code defects — concurrency saturation aborting Phase 1 parent screens, wall-clock budget exhaustion silently skipping children, a misleading `parse_failure` debug label that fires on successful calls, and in-main-slot child screens left pending. This forces manual re-audits and blocks releases. No single RCA quantifies these modes or ranks fixes.

## Users

- **Release operator** running an automated audit: needs reliable verdicts without manual re-audits.
- **Producer** reviewing audit results: needs trustworthy signals to make release decisions.
- **Agent** running audits: needs predictable behaviour and actionable failure diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A written RCA quantifies failure modes from at least 30 days of evidence, grouped by phase (Phase 1 parent, Phase 1 child, Phase 2 parent deep, Phase 2 child deep, false-positive screen) and by root cause, with reproducible commands/queries and representative examples.
2. The RCA explicitly confirms or refutes **F1** (the `parse_failure` label fires on successful calls) and states the effect on observability; it must distinguish label noise from genuine parse failures.
3. Every failure mode in the RCA is backed by a count and at least one concrete example (item id + log path or report excerpt).
4. A prioritised recommendation list is produced (impact × effort), each item naming the concrete change, the expected reliability effect, and the observable signal that would confirm improvement.
5. Recommendations cover, at minimum: JSON-output contract robustness (e.g. JSON-first prompting / schema retry / fenced-block tolerant parsing), timeout and wall-clock budget right-sizing, concurrency saturation and queue-wait policy, child-audit execution strategy (in-main-slot vs separate-process), provider-error retry policy, and debug-log observability (a correct, non-misleading reason taxonomy).
6. Each accepted recommendation is captured as a follow-up work item (child of this item or `discovered-from`) with its own testable ACs; rejected recommendations record the rationale.
7. UK English throughout; no code changes are required by this item other than producing the RCA/recommendations (implementation lands via the follow-ups).

## Constraints

- Read-only analysis of logs and stored reports; do not modify the audit runner as part of this item.
- Use bounded reads for large log stores (stream, filter by context/reason); never unbounded recursive grep over `.worklog/`.
- Do not close or reopen unrelated work items; link to the prior art below instead.

## Evidence Sources

1. **Debug corpus:** `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl` (91 files analysed; raw Pi streams + the logged `reason` field).
2. **Stored audit reports:** `wl show` worklog data (rawOutput per item; counts from 2026-09-15 export).
3. **Runner source:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_call_pi`, `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`, `_extract_json_array`, Phase 1/Phase 2 call sites).
4. **Log files:** `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/*.log` (audit runs with verdicts and diagnostics).

## Preliminary Findings (to be verified and extended)

### F1 — The debug-log `reason: parse_failure` label is misleading (observability bug)

**Confirmed.** Code inspection of `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` (L4828) shows:

```python
elif isinstance(result, dict) and (result.get("raw_stdout") or result.get("raw_stderr")):
    reason = "provider_error" if result.get("_provider_error") else "parse_failure"
```

The label fires whenever `raw_stdout` or `raw_stderr` is present — which is true on **every** successful call. Corpus analysis of 91 JSONL debug files shows:

- 91 files, all containing `parse_failure` entries as the dominant reason.
- Only 5 files contain `provider_error` (total: ~10 provider_error entries across the corpus).
- Only 2 files contain `debug_log` entries (explicit debug log path was provided).

The preliminary finding of ~92–95% false-positive rate is confirmed — the `parse_failure` label is an observability bug that invalidates any failure analysis keyed on it.

### F2 — Genuine JSON-contract failures are real but rare (~5–8%)

**To be verified.** The preliminary finding cites 34 genuine failures in 285 real-project logs. This count requires verification against the actual debug corpus — checking which `parse_failure` entries actually contain unparseable content vs. parseable content mislabelled by the F1 bug.

### F3 — Wall-clock budget exhaustion dominates (child skips + Phase 2 timeouts)

**Confirmed in log files.** Multiple log entries show:
- "pending deep code review (Phase 1 blocked)" — Phase 2 skipped after Phase 1 detected blocking issues.
- Parent-process timeout budgets vary widely (~120s, 900s, 1500s, 3110s) — inconsistent right-sizing.
- Stored report data (from prior audit): `Skipped due to audit timeout` ~176, `Audit runner skipped this child after Ns` ~100+.

### F4 — Concurrency saturation aborts Phase 1

**Confirmed.** Log files show repeated "Audit concurrency limit reached: audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated: no slot within 90s" and "Audit concurrency limit reached: semaphore 'audit' busy: no slot free within 0.0s (max_workers=1)". Phase 1 parent screens return `unmet` with zero Pi calls made.

### F5 — In-main-slot child screens leave children unverified

**Confirmed in log files.** Multiple entries show "pending deep code review (Phase 1 blocked)" — child ACs left in `partial (pending main-session review)` state when the main session does not run the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` prompts.

### F6 — Provider errors

**Confirmed.** Corpus analysis: ~10 `provider_error` entries across 91 files (SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ: 3, SA-0MSM6VU2K001IMVP: 1, SA-0MSUT8GQP004WSYN: 1, SA-0MSNYMKV7005P0H9: 1, SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42: 1). Provider errors are currently conflated with the misleading `parse_failure` label.

## Recommendations (Preliminary — to be finalised)

| Rec | Priority | Impact | Effort | Description | Follow-up Work Item |
|-----|----------|--------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| R1 | High | High | Low | Fix the debug-log reason taxonomy (observability) | SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99 (R1) |
| R2 | High | High | Medium | Harden JSON contract (JSON-first + tolerant + re-ask) | SA-0MU32TCFM003B78I (R2) |
| R3 | High | High | Medium | Right-size wall-clock budgets; stop silent child skips | SA-0MU32T6O0001UALR (R3) — in_review |
| R4 | High | High | Low-Medium | Priority queue for Phase 1 parent screen | SA-0MU32T8SH001R8MZ (R4) — in_review |
| R5 | Medium-High | High | Low | Enforce child-audit execution contract | SA-0MU32TE120012T49 (R5) |
| R6 | Medium | Medium | Low | Separate provider errors from parse failures | SA-0MU32TFKB0012ALC (R6) — blocked on R1 |
| R7 | Medium | Medium | Low | Emit per-run reliability summary | SA-0MU32TH89000YHP9 (R7) — blocked on R1, R6 |

## Related Work (Prior Art — all evaluated)

| Work Item | Title | Status | Relevance |
|-----------|-------|--------|-----------|
| SA-0MPOGKY8U007K206 | Add debug logging for Pi responses | completed | Introduced current reason label (root of F1) |
| SA-0MQ4GGKUR00752Z8 | Parse JSON array from mixed analysis+JSON | completed | Prior art for JSON contract (R2) |
| SA-0MRW8T054007QH0A | Audit runner bugs | completed | Prior art for JSON parse fallback |
| SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC | Consolidate duplicate Pi JSON parsers | **open, plan_complete** | Should be consulted before R2 implementation |
| SA-0MSF4AFXF000M5DN | Right-size parent-timeout guard | completed | Prior art for budget right-sizing (R3) |
| SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X | Configurable cumulative elapsed-time guard | completed | Prior art for timeout guards |
| SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL | Fail immediately on concurrency limit | completed | Prior art superseded by queue admission |
| SA-0MS0SQQTW006GNX9 | Phase 2 deep-analysis timeout | completed | Prior art for timeout issues |
| SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE | In-main-slot child audit mode | — | Prior art for R5 |
| SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 | Motivating audit (2026-09-15) | — | Source of this RCA |

## Existing State

The audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) has 10+ call sites for `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`. The debug-log reason taxonomy is set in a single branch (L4906) but is overly broad. The `_extract_json_array` parser exists but does not handle fenced blocks or prose-prefixed JSON consistently. Concurrency is managed via a priority queue with `max_workers=2` (configurable). Wall-clock budgets are set ad-hoc across multiple call sites.

## Desired Change

A comprehensive RCA documenting all failure modes with quantified counts, examples, and reproducible queries — followed by a prioritised recommendation list that feeds into the already-created follow-up work items (R1–R7).

## Key Files (predicted for RCA analysis)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — All call sites, timeout guards, concurrency, parse logic
- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl` — 91 debug log files (reason taxonomy analysis)
- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/*.log` — 100+ audit run log files (verdict/diagnostic analysis)
- `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` — Stored audit reports (rawOutput per item)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The 91 debug JSONL files and 100+ log files are representative of the 30-day evidence window required by AC1.
- **Assumption:** The preliminary counts (F1–F6) from the 2026-09-15 audit export are approximately correct and need refinement, not re-invention.
- **Risk:** The debug corpus may be incomplete — some audits may not have written debug files (e.g., early failures before debug logging was enabled).
- **Risk:** The existing child work items (R1–R7) may need revision based on findings — e.g., if R3 is confirmed as the dominant failure mode, its priority should be elevated.
- **Scope creep:** This is a read-only analysis item. Implementation work should only happen in the follow-up child work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does the debug corpus cover the required 30-day evidence window? — A: The 91 JSONL files span from 2026-08-12 to 2026-09-15 (~34 days), meeting the requirement.
- Q: Should the RCA include analysis of non-SorraAgents projects? — A: The RCA focuses on SorraAgents debug logs; other projects' debug logs can be consulted if patterns differ significantly.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** – Audit staleness race: post-persist comment bumps updatedAt past auditedAt — passed audits show stale icon (completed)
- **SA-0MSRMFSZL007CZVQ** – Documentation — update scope semantics (completed)
- **SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S** – Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (audits far too slow) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0msgeazmc009lhkl, 0msl1z70c007b9vz, 0msnymkv7005p0h9, 0mt2xrgeu0009qre, 0mu32t6o0001ualr (+349 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mt2xrgeu0009qre, 0mu32t6o0001ualr, 120s, 1500s, 3110s (+309 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: 0msnymkv7005p0h9, 0mt2xrgeu0009qre, aborts, acceptance, acs (+264 more)

# R1 — Audit debug log mislabels every successful call as `parse_failure`

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi_and_maybe_log` sets
`reason = "parse_failure"` whenever the Pi result carries `raw_stdout`/`raw_stderr`.
But `raw_stdout` is present on **every successful call**, so the debug log
labels successful calls as parse failures.

Evidence (2026-09-15 corpus scan):

- 19,663 `~/.audit_debug/**/audit_debug_*.jsonl` files; 39,619 entries with
  `reason: parse_failure` vs only 26 with `provider_error`.
- Re-running `extract_pi_text()` + `_extract_json_array()` over real-project
  logs (285 files) shows ~92-95% of `parse_failure` entries parse cleanly:
  `parent` 158/172, `phase2_deep` 93/98, `false-positive-screen` 41/43.
- Genuine parse failures in real-project logs: ~34.

Consequence: any failure analysis keyed on this label is invalid, and the
false funnel made the reliability RCA (SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL) far harder.

## Desired change

Replace the blanket label with an accurate taxonomy: a neutral default reason
(e.g. `call_trace`) for calls that returned, plus an explicit parse-outcome
flag set by the call site, and `parse_failure` only when the expected JSON
shape genuinely could not be extracted.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` no longer records `reason: parse_failure` for a
   call whose output was successfully parsed at the call site.
2. The debug entry carries an explicit parse-outcome field (e.g. `parse_ok:
   true|false`) and a neutral reason for successful calls.
3. A genuine parse failure is still recorded distinctly (labelled
   `parse_failure` or equivalent) and is machine-distinguishable from a
   successful call.
4. Provider errors remain labelled `provider_error` and are not conflated with
   parse failures.
5. Unit tests cover: successful call -> not `parse_failure`; genuine parse
   failure -> labelled; provider error -> `provider_error`.
6. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the reason taxonomy; existing
   debug-log tests/consumers are updated.
7. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Do not change audit verdict semantics; this is observability only.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`, call sites.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — debug-log taxonomy.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — debug-log tests.

## Evidence trail

- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0.jsonl` (labelled
  `parse_failure`, yet the screen produced valid classifications).

# R2 — Harden the audit JSON contract (JSON-first prompt + tolerant extraction + bounded re-ask)

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

Genuine JSON-contract failures are rarer than the debug label suggests
(~5-8%), but they are real and avoidable. In real-project logs, 34 genuine
failures; the dominant shape is the model stopping (`stopReason: stop`) after
narrative analysis and never emitting the required JSON array, with 16/34
producing <200 output tokens (empty or truncated text). Pi also routinely
wraps the array in Markdown code fences (```` ```json ... ``` ````) with prose
around it.

Prior art: SA-0MQ4GGKUR00752Z8 (parse mixed analysis+JSON),
SA-0MRW8T054007QH0A (JSON parse fallback), SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC (consolidate Pi
JSON parsers, open).

## Desired change

Make the JSON contract JSON-first and tolerant, and add a single bounded
"return only the JSON array" re-ask before the conservative `partial`
fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase 1 parent/child and Phase 2 parent/child prompts request the JSON
   array first (or only), with prose after, and restate the exact schema and
   the required keys.
2. `_extract_json_array` tolerates leading/trailing prose and Markdown code
   fences and selects the intended balanced array; covered by unit tests using
   real fenced/prose fixtures captured from the debug corpus.
3. On extraction failure, exactly one bounded re-ask ("return only the JSON
   array") is issued before falling back to `partial`; the re-ask is
   observable (context `verdict_reask`) and bounded by the per-call budget.
4. A genuine parse-failure rate is measured over a re-run corpus (>=20 items)
   and recorded on this item; it is reduced relative to the pre-change
   baseline.
5. Verdict semantics are unchanged: a persistent failure still falls back to
   the conservative `partial`, never `met`/`Yes`.
6. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- No project-specific commands; use the shared Pi utilities (`skill/scripts/pi_utils.py`)
  rather than adding a new parser (align with SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC).
- Evidence-scope cap (`--max-citations-per-ac`) must remain honoured.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_extract_json_array`, Phase 1/2
  prompts, `verdict_reask` handling.
- `skill/scripts/pi_utils.py` — `extract_pi_text`.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — parser fixtures/tests.

# R5 — Enforce the child-audit execution contract (no silent pending child screens)

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

With the default `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT=true`
(SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE), the runner emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` prompts
for the main session instead of executing child screens. If the session does
not run them, child ACs remain `partial (pending main-session review)` and the
parent cannot close — with no explicit gate or resume. The 2026-09-15 audit of
SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 ended in exactly this state.

## Desired change

Define and enforce the child-audit execution contract so a parent audit either
completes all child verdicts or surfaces an explicit, actionable, resumable
gate — never a silent `partial`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The contract is documented in `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`: either the runner executes child
   screens itself, or in-main-slot mode must surface an explicit
   "N child screens pending" gate that prevents a `Yes` verdict and closure.
2. A parent audit never ends with child ACs `partial (pending main-session
   review)` presented as a normal result: the pending state is explicit,
   actionable (names the child ids and how to complete them), and blocks
   `Ready to close: Yes`.
3. A persisted/resumable signal records which child screens remain, so a
   subsequent run completes them without a full re-audit.
4. Tests cover both modes: separate-process executes the child screens;
   in-main-slot emits the gate and the parent cannot report `Yes` with pending
   children.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Do not silently change the default mode; make whichever default is chosen
  safe (explicit gate or in-process execution).

# Objective

Interview-driven skills (intake, plan) must require the agent to state its **preferred option explicitly** — with a short rationale — for every clarifying question/round, so operators can accept a recommendation at a glance instead of evaluating bare option lists.

## Problem statement

Agents running the interview-driven skills (`intake`, `plan`) ask clarifying questions and present options, but the skills never require the agent to say which option it prefers. Operators must therefore assess every option themselves and frequently reply "what do you recommend?", adding round-trips. The agent's reasoning is also left implicit. Requiring an explicit preferred option (clearly marked as a recommendation) makes interviews faster and keeps the agent's reasoning visible, without removing the operator's choice.

## Users

AI agents conducting interviews, and producers/operators answering them.

**User stories:**

- As a producer answering an intake or plan interview, I want the agent to tell me which option it prefers and why, so that I can accept it immediately or override it with full context.
- As an AI agent following the skill instructions, I want one explicit rule on how to phrase recommendations, so that I apply it consistently in every interview round.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/intake/SKILL.md` (Interview section and interview-style hard requirement) requires the agent to state its preferred option for each interview question/round, using a consistent marker such as `**Recommended:** <option> — <one-line rationale>`.
2. `skill/plan/SKILL.md` (Interview section and interview-style hard requirement) states the same requirement with the same marker.
3. The wording makes clear the recommendation is **advisory**: the operator may choose any option, and the agent proceeds with the operator's choice (no unilateral selection and no auto-selecting the recommendation without confirmation).
4. The requirement applies to every interview round and to the producer-review handoff (questions routed via `wl reviewed`), not only the first round.
5. A doc-hygiene test asserts the recommendation requirement is present in both skill docs (e.g. `tests/test_interview_recommendation.py` asserting the marker/instruction text in both `SKILL.md` files).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline (`skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js`). Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Scope is skill markdown plus one doc-hygiene test; no changes to `wl`, runtime scripts, or work-item data.
- Must not conflict with `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, which explicitly forbids asking the user what to refactor — refactor is not an interview skill and is out of scope.
- Wording must stay concise and consistent with the existing style of both skills (short bullets, no new sub-structures).
- The consolidation of interview conduct into a shared interview skill is tracked separately as **SA-0MUBVM6FR000NDI1**; this item must deliver the behaviour without waiting for that refactor.

## Existing state

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` § "Hard requirements" has "Interview style: concise, high-signal questions, max three per round." and § "4. Interview" describes the interview loop — neither requires an explicit recommendation.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` § "Hard requirements" has "Use concise interview style: ≤3 high-signal questions per iteration; prefer multiple-choice but allow freeform." and § "3. Interview" — neither requires an explicit recommendation.
- There is **no** shared interview skill or module: no `skill/interview/` directory, and no `interview`/`Interview` class or function in `skill/shared/` (interviews are agent-driven prose, not scripted).

## Desired change

1. In `skill/intake/SKILL.md`:
   - Add to the interview-style hard requirement: the agent must state its preferred option explicitly (with a one-line rationale) for every question/round, marked `**Recommended:**`.
   - Reinforce in § "4. Interview" that the recommendation is advisory and the operator's choice always wins.
2. In `skill/plan/SKILL.md`:
   - Apply the identical requirement to the interview-style hard requirement and § "3. Interview".
3. Add a doc-hygiene test asserting both skill docs contain the recommendation requirement.

## Key Files:

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add the explicit-preferred-option rule to the interview-style hard requirement and the § 4 Interview section.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Add the same rule to the interview-style hard requirement and the § 3 Interview section.
- `tests/test_interview_recommendation.py` — New doc-hygiene test asserting the recommendation requirement text appears in both `SKILL.md` files.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — Reflect the interview-conduct requirement if maintainer-facing reference detail is added.
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — Same for the plan skill.

## Related work

### Potentially related work items

- **SA-0MUBVM6FR000NDI1** — "Refactor intake and plan to share a common interview skill" (`open`, high): the separate refactor item requested alongside this one; consolidates the interview conduct that this item amends.
- **SA-0MRIIQLQ800788MC** — "Refactor command/intake.md for conciseness" (`completed`): previous pass over intake interview guidance.
- **SA-0MS3CIU0F00066CD** — "Move /intake command to be a skill" (`completed`): established `skill/intake/SKILL.md` as the live interview process.
- **SA-0MRW7ER4L000SK8Z** — "Shared status lifecycle helper for skills" (`completed`): precedent for extracting shared skill behaviour into `skill/shared/`.

### Potentially related docs

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — the intake interview process.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — the plan interview process.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — explicitly non-interactive; confirms the boundary of "any skill".
- `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — existing pattern for doc-hygiene tests over `SKILL.md` content.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPDZDVG00013CQJ** – Implement: Agent push-to-dev behavior (completed)
- **SA-0MPGX3ZQ7006S6HN** – Implementation Model Routing (completed)
- **SA-0MQS1V0YJ002LI2F** – IntakeAll: /intake subprocess invocation appears to hang (false alarm) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: action, agent, always, applies, driven (+14 more)
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — matched: action, agent, always, driven, intake (+13 more)
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — matched: action, agent, always, explicitly, intake (+13 more)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** A recommendation could be misread as the agent deciding unilaterally. Mitigation: AC #3 explicitly states the recommendation is advisory and the operator's choice wins.
- **Risk:** Scope creep into building the shared interview skill. Mitigation: that work is tracked separately as SA-0MUBVM6FR000NDI1; this item only amends the two skill docs plus a test.
- **Risk:** Both skills must be updated, allowing drift if only one is changed. Mitigation: AC #5 asserts both, and the shared-skill refactor follows.
- **Assumption:** Prose instructions in `SKILL.md` are the correct place to change agent interview behaviour, because interviews are agent-driven and not scripted (no runtime interview module exists).
- **Assumption:** Priority `high` is adopted for this item too, following the operator's `--priority high` directive on the intake command.
- **Assumption:** The `**Recommended:**` marker wording is an implementation detail; implementers may choose an equivalent explicit marker provided it is consistent across both skills.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked — the operator's seed intent ("when conducting interviews in any skill the agent should always recommend their preferred action explicitly") was sufficiently specific to draft the brief directly.

Decisions taken with the operator's stated recommendations (per the new rule this item introduces):

- **Ordering — Recommended:** implement this item first (small, independently deliverable), then the shared-interview-skill refactor (SA-0MUBVM6FR000NDI1). Rationale: delivers the behaviour immediately and the refactor then preserves it.
- **Scope — Recommended:** amend both `intake` and `plan` now rather than waiting for the shared skill. Rationale: the shared-skill item is higher-risk and should not gate this behaviour change.

# Objective

Extract a single canonical interview skill that `intake` and `plan` both reference for interview conduct, removing the duplicated interview prose that currently drifts between the two skills.

## Problem statement

There is no common interview skill. `skill/intake/SKILL.md` (§ 4 Interview) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` (§ 3 Interview) each define their own interview process in prose, duplicating guidance on question limits (≤3 per round), multiple-choice preference, producer-review handoff (`wl reviewed`), and appendix recording. Every enhancement must be applied twice and can silently diverge — the preferred-option rule added by **SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ** is the most recent example.

## Users

Skill maintainers and the AI agents that execute the intake and plan interviews.

**User stories:**

- As a skill maintainer, I want one canonical definition of interview conduct, so that I can change it once and both skills pick it up.
- As an AI agent running an interview, I want a single unambiguous interview contract to follow, so that my behaviour is identical in intake and plan.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A canonical interview component exists (proposed: `skill/interview/SKILL.md`, marked `disable-model-invocation: true`), defining at minimum: ≤3 high-signal questions per round, multiple-choice preferred with freeform allowed, the explicit `**Recommended:** <option>` preferred-option rule (from SA-0MUBVLFP70064SPJ), the producer-review handoff via `wl reviewed`, and idempotent appendix recording of questions/answers.
2. `skill/intake/SKILL.md` and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` reference the shared component instead of restating the interview rules, with no duplication left behind.
3. No interview behaviour is lost or changed beyond consolidation: the requirements listed in AC #1 remain enforced through the shared component.
4. A test asserts both skills reference the shared component and that the shared component contains each required interview rule.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline (`skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js`). Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Follow existing skill-authoring conventions: YAML frontmatter, `$(skill_path <name>)` runtime resolution, and `docs/dev/<skill>-reference.md` for deep reference detail.
- Do not break the scripts/import conventions documented in `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`.

## Existing state

- Interview prose is duplicated in `skill/intake/SKILL.md` § 4 and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` § 3, plus interview-style bullets in each skill's Hard requirements section.

## Desired change

1. Create `skill/interview/SKILL.md` as the canonical interview contract (hidden helper skill).
2. Replace the duplicated interview prose in `skill/intake/SKILL.md` and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` with a reference to the shared component, retaining only skill-specific interview inputs (e.g. seed context, what to capture per feature).
3. Add a test asserting the shared component exists, is referenced by both skills, and contains the required rules.
4. Update maintainer docs.

## Key Files:

- `skill/interview/SKILL.md` — New canonical interview conduct (question limits, multiple-choice preference, explicit preferred-option recommendation, producer-review handoff, appendix recording).
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Replace duplicated interview prose with a reference to the shared component.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Replace duplicated interview prose with a reference to the shared component.
- `tests/test_interview_skill_shared.py` — New test asserting the shared component exists, both skills reference it, and required rules are present.

## Related work

### Potentially related work items

- **SA-0MRW7ER4L000SK8Z** — "Shared status lifecycle helper for skills" (`completed`): precedent and pattern for extracting shared skill behaviour.
- **SA-0MRIIQLQ800788MC** — "Refactor command/intake.md for conciseness" (`completed`): previous consolidation of intake interview guidance.

# Fix inherited_pass bypass: three fixes in audit_runner.py

## Summary
The audit runner incorrectly allows `inherited_pass` to bypass the pre-review stage block, producing false-positive "Ready to close: Yes" verdicts. This task combines three related fixes in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`.

## Fix 1: inherited_pass assignment (line ~9897)

In the `if not parent_gaps:` branch, add a stage guard so `inherited_pass=True` is only applied to children already in `in_review` or `done` stage. Pre-review children (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) must not receive `inherited_pass` — they must be audited independently.

- Code at ~9897 checks child stage before setting `inherited_pass = True`
- Only children with `stage` in `("in_review", "done")` receive `inherited_pass`
- Pre-review stage children skip the `inherited_pass` branch and proceed to independent audit
- Existing `_child_content_changed` guard is preserved

## Fix 2: all_children_reviewed check (line ~4207)

The `all_children_reviewed` check currently allows `inherited_pass` to exempt a child from the stage check:

```python
all_children_reviewed = all(
    c.get("stage") in ("in_review", "done") or c.get("inherited_pass")
    for c in active_children
)
```

Remove `or c.get("inherited_pass")` — the stage check should be independent. The `inherited_pass` flag affects the verdict, not the stage blocking logic.

- `all_children_reviewed` only checks child stages, not `inherited_pass`
- A child at `intake_complete` with `inherited_pass=True` is correctly counted as blocking
- Existing exempt-child logic (deleted, completed/done) is preserved

## Fix 3: summary text (line ~4333)

The summary unconditionally appends "All children are in in_review or done stage." when `all_children_reviewed` is true. Fix this so the line is only emitted when that statement is actually true; otherwise, the summary names the blocking children.

- The "All children are in in_review or done stage." line is only emitted when all active children are actually in those stages
- When children block closure, the summary names them
- No regression on existing "Ready to close: No" cases that already name blocking children

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All three fixes applied in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- [ ] Regression test passes (separate task SA-0MUD5OMQG0068P4I)
- [ ] No regression on existing tests
- [ ] Existing `_child_content_changed` guard preserved

# Voice-to-text pi extension using faster-whisper (Ctrl+Space)

## Problem statement

Pi has no voice input, so operators must type long prompts by hand. We need a pi
extension that captures microphone audio, transcribes it locally with
[faster-whisper](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper), streams the text
into the pi editor, and submits it automatically — toggled with a single
shortcut key.

## Users

Primary user: pi operators running the TUI on Linux/WSL2 with a CUDA GPU (the
requesting operator has an RTX 3050, 4 GB VRAM). Secondary user: any pi operator
who wants hands-free prompt entry.

Example user stories:

- As a pi operator, I press **Ctrl+Space**, speak my prompt, and it appears in
  the editor live, so I can dictate instead of typing.
- As a pi operator, when I stop speaking for a moment or press **Ctrl+Space**
  again, the prompt is sent exactly as if I had typed it and pressed Enter, so I
  don't have to touch the keyboard to submit.
- As a privacy-conscious operator, transcription runs entirely on my own
  machine (local GPU), so my audio never leaves my system.
- As an operator without CUDA, I can fall back to CPU inference by changing one
  setting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In the pi TUI, pressing **Ctrl+Space** (configurable keybinding) starts
   microphone capture; the footer/status area shows a clear recording indicator.
2. While recording, partial transcription results are streamed into the pi
   editor and each new partial replaces the previous one; on completion the
   editor contains the final transcript.
3. Recording stops and the transcript is **submitted automatically** when
   either (a) Ctrl+Space is pressed again, or (b) the user has been silent for
   more than 3 seconds (configurable). Submission behaves the same as if the
   operator had typed the text and pressed Enter (a normal user message,
   respecting pi's busy/steering mode).
4. Transcription is performed locally by faster-whisper on the CUDA GPU
   (`float16`) through a persistent Python worker that loads the model once per
   session; model size, device and compute type are configurable
   (default: `small` + `cuda` + `float16`, with automatic CPU `int8` fallback
   when CUDA is unavailable).
5. Audio is captured as 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM through a configurable capture
   command (default works under WSLg/PulseAudio); if a required dependency is
   missing the extension shows an actionable notification and never crashes the
   pi session.
6. Unit tests cover the recording state machine, silence/pause detection,
   partial-transcript replacement, the Ctrl+Space toggle, and the worker
   protocol — without requiring a real microphone or GPU (capture and
   transcription are mocked).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **TypeScript extension**, consistent with `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals`
  (jiti-loaded, no build step). Must use only the public `ExtensionAPI`.
- **Python bridge**: faster-whisper is Python-only, so the extension spawns a
  long-lived Python worker and talks to it over a line-delimited JSON protocol
  (model loaded once, not per utterance).
- **Platform**: Linux/WSL2 with CUDA. GPU target is an RTX 3050 with 4 GB VRAM —
  the default model must fit comfortably (`small`); `large-v3` may OOM and is
  not the default.
- **Local-only**: no cloud/network STT; privacy is a hard requirement.
- **Keybinding conflict risk**: Ctrl+Space is commonly intercepted by terminals
  and Windows IMEs, so the keybinding must be configurable and documented, with
  a recommended alternative.
- **WSL audio caveat**: WSL2 audio input requires WSLg/PulseAudio (or an
  ALSA→Pulse bridge). Capture backend must be selectable/overridable rather
  than hard-coded.

## Existing state

- Pi extension infrastructure already exists in this repo: `pi-client/` holds
  pi client extensions (`proxy-sse-signals`, `proxy-compaction-bridge`), each
  symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` and unit-tested under `tests/unit/`
  with `node:test` (see `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs`).
- The required pi APIs are available: `pi.registerShortcut(Key.ctrl("space"), …)`,
  `ctx.ui.setEditorText()/getEditorText()`, `ctx.ui.setStatus()`,
  `ctx.ui.notify()`, and `pi.sendUserMessage()`.
- Related precedent: the **speak** skill (`SA-0MRHSXIT00089DQ3`) is the inverse
  (text-to-speech) direction and uses a similar external-process bridge.
- faster-whisper is **not** installed in this environment. `arecord` exists but
  the current environment reports *no soundcards*; `ffmpeg`, `sox`, `parecord`
  and `pactl` are absent.
- No existing voice-input/STT work item or code (searched worklog and repo).

## Desired change

Add a new pi extension `pi-client/voice-input/` that:

1. Registers a configurable shortcut (default `Ctrl+Space`) that toggles
   recording.
2. Spawns a capture process (configurable; WSLg/PulseAudio-friendly default)
   producing 16 kHz mono PCM, and frames it for both transcription and
   energy-based silence detection.
3. Runs a persistent `faster-whisper` Python worker on the GPU, feeding
   accumulated audio to produce live partial transcripts.
4. Updates the pi editor live, shows a recording status indicator, and submits
   the final transcript (or leaves an error notification) when the stop trigger
   fires.
5. Ships a dependency/doctor check (faster-whisper import, CUDA availability,
   capture backend, model presence) that emits actionable guidance.
6. Includes docs (`docs/dev/voice-input.md`, extension `README.md`) and unit
   tests (`tests/unit/test-voice-input.mjs`), and is installable by symlink into
   `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `pi-client/voice-input/index.ts` — ExtensionAPI entry: shortcut registration, recording state machine, editor updates, auto-send, status/notifications.
- `pi-client/voice-input/recorder.ts` — spawns the capture command, frames 16 kHz PCM, computes per-frame RMS, drives silence/pause detection.
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — persistent worker lifecycle and line-delimited JSON protocol (start/feed/finalise/stop).
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — loads faster-whisper once (device/compute type from config) and transcribes incoming PCM chunks.
- `pi-client/voice-input/config.ts` — resolves settings/env (keybinding, model, device, compute type, silence threshold/ms, capture command).
- `pi-client/voice-input/doctor.ts` — preflight dependency/CUDA/backend/model checks with actionable messages.
- `pi-client/voice-input/README.md` — install, WSL/CUDA prerequisites, usage, troubleshooting.
- `docs/dev/voice-input.md` — design, protocol, configuration reference.
- `tests/unit/test-voice-input.mjs` — unit tests for the state machine, silence detection, partial replacement, toggle, and protocol.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — (optional) symlink the new extension into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRHSXIT00089DQ3` — Create a speak skill for text-to-speech (TTS) audio generation and playback (inverse direction; precedent for an external-process audio bridge).
- `SA-0MTWOYFLU004LB2R` — Add TTS to the standup skill (related audio tooling).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLQ904LV1D1V8ZW** – Unit Tests and Manual E2E Script (completed)
- **SA-0MPKYR7SS000CO2J** – Ralph status command produces inconsistent reports (completed)
- **SA-0MKYE40VG1V2DTOX** – Agent error: 'wl show --thread' missing when running /impplement (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: again, auto, captures, com, create (+11 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: again, auto, com, create, extension (+8 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: auto, com, create, editor, extension (+8 more)

> Note: the automated matches above are keyword-frequency noise (audit tooling,
> unrelated Ralph/status items); the manually curated entries are the
> genuinely related work.

## Risks and assumptions

- **VRAM limit (4 GB)** — `large-v3` may OOM; default `small` and document
  model trade-offs. *Mitigation*: automatic CPU `int8` fallback + clear errors.
- **WSL audio fragility** — capture may fail without WSLg/PulseAudio. *Mitigation*:
  configurable capture command + doctor check + actionable notification.
- **Ctrl+Space interception** — terminal/IME may swallow the key. *Mitigation*:
  configurable keybinding, documented alternative, `/voice-input` command fallback.
- **Partial-transcription latency** — naive re-transcription of a growing buffer
  can be slow. *Mitigation*: bounded sliding window / periodic cadence; tune in
  implementation.
- **Assumption**: "same as if I typed it" means the transcript is submitted as a
  normal user message via `pi.sendUserMessage()`, honouring pi's current
  steering/follow-up mode when busy.
- **Assumption**: live partial text is desired (the operator compared behaviour
  to typing), so partials update the editor while speaking.
- **Scope-creep risk**: multi-language selection, speaker diarisation,
  wake-word activation and cloud STT are explicitly out of scope; capture them
  as separate work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which faster-whisper model/hardware should be the default? — Answer
  (operator): "Yes I have a GPU CUDA to target". Research: `nvidia-smi` in this
  environment reports an NVIDIA RTX 3050 with 4 GB VRAM and CUDA 13.2 driver.
  Default chosen: `small` + `cuda` + `float16`, with CPU `int8` fallback.
  Source: interactive reply + `nvidia-smi`.
- Q: Platform scope — Linux-only or cross-platform? — Answer (operator): "We can
  target Linux with WSL". Research: `arecord` present but no soundcard detected
  here; WSLg/PulseAudio is the expected capture path. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: When auto-send fires while pi is busy, should it steer, queue, or stay in
  the editor? — Answer (operator): "The behavior when sending should be the same
  as if I typed it in". Interpretation: submit as a normal user message and let
  pi's configured steering/follow-up mode apply. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Should partial text stream live into the editor, or appear only on stop? —
  Answer (operator, implied by "same as if I typed it in"): live partial text.
  This is a documented assumption; revisit if undesired. Source: interactive
  reply (implicit).

## Post-audit recovery note (2026-09-27, audit run 2178s)

The automated `/skill:audit` run on 2026-09-26 failed for **infrastructure
reasons**, not because of any defect in the voice-input work:

- The local proxy was in `cheap` mode (`AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1`) while several
  audits ran concurrently; the Phase 1 parent screen fell back to `partial`
  because the audit concurrency queue saturated (no slot within 90s).
- The Phase 2 deep-analysis output could not be parsed (all 8 ACs marked
  `partial`) and the test-failure child's Phase 2 deep analysis timed out.
- The generated `Ready to close: No` verdict is therefore
  **fallback-tainted (not a genuine model assessment)** and the runner was
  required to restore the pre-audit state rather than demote.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle transition then failed with
  `Invalid status/stage combination: status "blocked" is not compatible with
  stage "in_review"`, leaving the item `blocked`/`in_review`. It has been
  recovered manually to `blocked`/`plan_complete`.

Side effects of the failed run (documented for the producer):

- The full project suite was **red** at the audited HEAD (4 commands, 11
  failures, all in the audit/test infrastructure); triage created 11 critical
  `test-failure` items and linked
  `SA-0MUIXZKH500624QM` as a blocking child/dependency of this item.
- The failed parent audit persisted short `Ready to close: No` child audits
  to the five voice-input children (because they carry no parseable AC
  heading), which reverted them from `completed`/`in_review` to
  `open`/`plan_complete` (two now `blocked`). Their implementation is
  complete and merged to `dev`.

This note intentionally changes the description hash so the stored
fallback-tainted audit becomes stale: **re-run the audit with `--force`**
(and preferably when the proxy is not saturated and the suite is green).

# Ship report to Discord needs titling

## Problem statement

The Discord ship report embed title is hardcoded as `Release vX.Y.Z` and does not include the project name from the worklog config. Additionally, the report description should include the project name for clarity.

## Users

- **Release operator**: Wants the Discord notification to clearly identify which project is being released, especially when monitoring multiple project releases.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Discord embed title changes from `Release vX.Y.Z` to `<ProjectName> Release vX.Y.Z`, where `<ProjectName>` is read from the worklog config's `projectName` field.
2. The project name is resolved from `<project>/.worklog/config.yaml` (same config path used for webhook URL resolution), with fallback to the global config `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`.
3. If the config is missing or `projectName` is absent, the title gracefully falls back to `Release vX.Y.Z`.
4. The embed description includes the project name alongside the version for added clarity.
5. All existing unit tests pass, with updated assertions reflecting the new title format.

## Constraints

- Non-breaking change — existing webhook behaviour must not be affected.
- The YAML parser (`parseSimpleYaml`) already handles top-level `projectName` keys.
- Must use the same config resolution precedence as the webhook URL (project config first, then global).

## Existing state

- `buildDiscordPayload()` in `discord-notify.js` hardcodes the title: `title: Release v${versionText}`.
- The `parseSimpleYaml()` function already parses `projectName` from config (verified in tests).
- `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl()` already follows the correct precedence pattern.
- The `sendReleaseNotification()` function resolves the webhook URL but does not read `projectName`.

## Desired change

1. Add a `resolveProjectName(projectRoot)` helper (parallel to `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl`) that reads `projectName` from the worklog config.
2. Update `sendReleaseNotification()` to resolve the project name and pass it to `buildDiscordPayload()`.
3. Update `buildDiscordPayload()` to accept a `projectName` parameter and include it in the embed title and description.

## Key Files

- `scripts/discord-notify.js` — Add project name resolution and update payload builder
- `tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — Update title assertions from `Release v1.2.3` to `<ProjectName> Release v1.2.3`

## Related work

- `WL-0MUB023JP001A9N3` — This work item itself (ship skill Discord notification)

## Note on bot name

The "bot name" that appears in Discord messages is controlled by the webhook URL configuration within Discord's channel settings, not by application code. This cannot be fixed programmatically — it requires configuring the webhook's display name in Discord. The fix addresses what CAN be controlled: the embed title and description content.

Create `pi-client/voice-input/recorder.ts` — audio capture and silence detection.

**Responsibilities:**
- Spawn the configurable capture command (default: arecord -f S16_LE -r 16000 -c 1) as a child process
- Read raw 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM from stdout in fixed-size frames (e.g. 160 bytes = 10 ms)
- Compute per-frame RMS energy for silence/pause detection
- Emit data events with PCM frame buffers + RMS value
- Track silence: emit silence event after configurable idle duration (default 3 s)
- Track pause: emit pause event when silence exceeds a longer threshold (e.g. 2 s) for partial transcription triggers
- Handle capture process exit: emit error with actionable message
- Graceful shutdown: send SIGINT to capture process on stop

**Key APIs:**
- child_process.spawn() for capture command
- Node.js Readable stream for PCM framing
- RMS computation on 16-bit PCM samples

**Unit tests (TDD — no real microphone; feed synthetic PCM):**
- RMS computation over known 16-bit sample buffers
- Silence fires after exactly the configured idle duration (deterministic clock)
- Speech keeps the silence timer reset; mixed speech/silence sequences
- Pause event cadence for partial transcription
- Capture process exit surfaces an actionable error, never throws

Create the whisper worker protocol — persistent Python worker and TypeScript client.

**Files:**
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — TypeScript client
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — Python worker process

**whisper-client.ts responsibilities:**
- Spawn whisper_worker.py with configurable model/device/compute args
- Implement line-delimited JSON protocol (worker reads stdin, writes JSONL to stdout)
- Protocol messages: START (model init), FEED (PCM chunk), FINALISE (get transcript), STOP
- Handle partial transcripts: emit events as they arrive
- Handle errors: forward worker stderr/exit code as error events
- Lifecycle: init on recording start, feed PCM frames during recording, finalise on stop, clean exit

**whisper_worker.py responsibilities:**
- Import faster-whisper on startup
- Load model once (device + compute_type from config, with CPU int8 fallback)
- Run a loop: read JSON commands from stdin, write JSON responses to stdout
- FEED accumulates audio, transcribes at configurable cadence
- FINALISE returns the complete transcript
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM

**Unit tests (TDD — mock the Python worker process):**
- START message spawns worker and waits for READY response
- FEED messages buffer data and trigger partial transcript callbacks
- FINALISE collects all buffered data and returns final transcript
- STOP sends SHUTDOWN, waits for ACK, verifies clean exit
- Worker stderr/exit code produces error events, never crashes the client

# Intake Brief: Remote `dev` corrupted by test fixtures (test isolation bug)

## Problem Statement

Running the full test suite from the live main checkout (`run_tests.py --scope full`)
mutated the production repository: local `dev` HEAD was moved to fixture commits,
~59 fixture commits and stray branches were created, `.git` config (identity,
`core.bare`, `core.hooksPath`) was rewritten, tracked `.githooks/*` files were
deleted, and fixture commits were **pushed to the real `origin/dev`** —
destroying the real `dev` history. The remote has since been force-restored, but
the underlying test-isolation defect is unfixed and can recur.

## Users & User Stories

- **Agent / operator:** "When I run the full suite (or the pre-push gate) from the
  live checkout, my repository must be left byte-for-byte unchanged — no branch,
  ref, worktree, or `.git/config` mutation."
- **Team / reviewer:** "If a test ever mutates the live repository, the run must
  fail immediately and name the culprit test, so we never silently ship fixture
  commits to `origin/dev` again."
- **Future maintainer:** "Every test that shells out to real `git` must use an
  isolated sandbox, with a documented, enforced convention I can follow."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Hermetic git usage:** every test helper that runs real `git` commands
  (repo creation, `branch -M`, worktree add, `remote add`, `push`) operates inside
  a `tmp_path`-rooted sandbox and asserts it is not targeting the main checkout.
  Helpers carry `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_CONFIG_*`/identity isolation where
  needed. *Verification:* code review of every real-git helper + a regression test
  per helper asserting the sandbox invariant.
- **AC2 — Deterministic reproduction / guard-fires proof:** a documented, ordered
  invocation deterministically demonstrates the leak (or, if the exact leak proves
  non-reproducible, an executable proof that the new guard fires on a simulated
  live-repo mutation). *Verification:* reproduced in ≥3 consecutive runs and the
  command + captured signature recorded as a comment on this work item.
- **AC3 — Regression guard:** `run_tests.py --scope full` snapshots the main
  checkout's `git for-each-ref` and local `.git/config` before and after the run
  and fails the run if either changed; a root autouse session-scoped conftest
  fixture does the same for direct `pytest` invocations and names the offending
  test. *Verification:* a dedicated test simulates a ref/config mutation and
  asserts the guard fails (both entry points).
- **AC4 — Live checkout left clean:** the main checkout contains no fixture
  branches/refs and no `root-file-repo/` after the fix; cleanup of the existing
  artefacts is delivered by the spun-off companion item `SA-0MUG216UP008821M`
  (blocked by this item; verify it completes and `git for-each-ref` shows no
  fixture refs).
- **AC5 — Documentation:** test-authoring documentation states the hermetic-git
  requirement and the guard behaviour, with a worked example. *Verification:*
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` and `skill/test/SKILL.md` updated.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes, zero new
  regressions; no test is skipped, xfailed, or retried to reach green.

## Constraints

- The guard must not false-positive on legitimate `tmp_path` repositories,
  worktrees created under `tmp_path`, or the live checkout's own agent worktrees
  (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-*`).
- No global sleeps, no whole-suite serialisation, no single-worker requirement.
- The fix must not push to the real `origin`; all implementation happens in the
  `implement.py start` worktree.
- The live-checkout cleanup (stale branches, `root-file-repo/`, stale tmp
  worktrees) must not disturb other agents' worktrees or unrelated branches, and
  must retain the `backup-*` tags for rollback.
- Minimal blast radius: change shared helpers only where required and re-verify
  the full suite if a shared helper changes.

  (`6d7b4b4f` + `SA-0MTC5CRVI008RD1K` install_pi fix) — see the incident comment.

# Guard contract tests and guard-fires proof

## Goal

Author the failing-first tests that pin the sandbox invariant, the snapshot/compare contract,
and both guard entry points — including the executable proof that the guard fires on a
live-repo mutation (F1 AC4 fallback; parent AC2 + AC3 verification).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (sandbox)** Unit tests for `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` prove: a target path inside any
  git work tree is rejected; a `tmp_path` directory is accepted; a repo created by the factory
  resolves `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` under `tmp_path`; a migrated fixture repo has no
  remote pointing at the repository's real `origin`. *Verification:* `pytest skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`.
- **AC2 (snapshot contract)** Unit tests prove the snapshot/compare helper reports: an added ref,
  a deleted ref, a moved ref (e.g. `refs/heads/dev` advanced), a changed local `.git/config` key,
  a deleted tracked file, and a newly added untracked non-ignored top-level entry — and reports
  nothing for an unchanged repo. *Verification:* same test module.
- **AC3 (guard-fires proof — conftest entry point)** A subprocess test runs pytest **as the
  session root** inside a `tmp_path` git repo whose single test mutates that repo (creates a
  branch); the guard aborts the session non-zero and names the offending test. The nested repo
  arms the guard via its own conftest included from the shared plugin module. *Verification:*
  `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`.
- **AC4 (guard-fires proof — run_tests entry point)** A subprocess test runs
  `run_tests.py` against a `tmp_path` git repo whose configured test command mutates a ref; the
  run exits non-zero. *Verification:* same test module.
- **AC5 (no false positives)** A test that creates branches/worktrees in an unrelated `tmp_path`
  repo does NOT trip the guard, and a no-op run reports clean. Covers the parent constraint that
  legitimate `tmp_path` repositories and `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` agent worktrees must not
  false-positive.
- **AC6 (red is behavioural)** Before F3-F5 land, the tests fail for behavioural reasons (missing
  attribute / raised `RuntimeError` / non-zero exit), not with a bare collection error caused by a
  missing module; the module ships documented stubs raising `NotImplementedError` if needed.
- **AC7** No source-text/grep assertions: the tests assert observable behaviour only (per
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern 1).

- **Covers parent **AC1 — Hermetic git usage:** every test helper that runs real `git` commands
- **Covers parent **AC3 — Regression guard:** `run_tests.py --scope full` snapshots the main


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` (new) — sandbox + snapshot contract tests.
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` (new) — both guard entry points, guard-fires proof, no-false-positive test.

## Notes

- "Red before F3-F5, green after" is intentionally NOT an AC here (unverifiable at close);
  F3/F4/F5 each own "its slice is green" and F7 owns whole-suite green.
- Mutating the live checkout to obtain the proof is forbidden; the guard is tested in a
  subprocess whose session root is a `tmp_path` repo.

# Hermetic git sandbox helper and migration

## Goal

Provide one shared, acyclic helper for hermetic real-git fixtures (sandbox assertion, env
isolation, repo/remote/worktree factories, snapshot/compare) and route every real-git test
helper through it. Satisfies parent AC1 and provides the snapshot API used by F4/F5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` exists, is **stdlib-only** (no `shared.*` or
  `test.*` imports), and exposes: `assert_outside_git_worktree(path)`, an env-isolated git
  runner (clears/overrides `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`,
  and sets fixture author/committer identity), `init_repo`, `init_bare_remote`, `add_worktree`,
  `snapshot_repo_state(root)` and `diff_snapshots(before, after)`.
- **AC2** `assert_outside_git_worktree` raises a clear error for any path resolving inside a git
  work tree that is not rooted at the sandbox root — including paths nested inside an enclosing
  repository (superset of the existing `_init_repo` guard, which it replaces).
- **AC3** All real-git helpers route through the helper: `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo`
  and `_make_real_git_project_with_worktree`
  (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py`), `_make_real_repo`
  (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py`), `_make_repo`
  (`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`), plus the remaining real-`git init` helpers in
  `skill/shared/tests/test_skill_extensions.py` and `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_fresh_repo_e2e.py`.
- **AC4** Every migrated fixture repo is created under `tmp_path`; its `git rev-parse
  --show-toplevel` resolves under `tmp_path`, and it has no remote pointing at the repository's
  real `origin`. *Verification:* behaviour-based per-helper assertions in F2 AC1 (NOT a source grep).
- **AC5** `snapshot_repo_state` uses read-only plumbing only (`for-each-ref`,
  `config --local --list`, `worktree list`, `status --porcelain=v1 -uall`) and never runs `gc`,
  `update-index`, `fetch` or `--refresh`; the untracked surface is `git status -uall`

  lists `.pytest_cache/`/`.ruff_cache/`).

  (registered worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/`) — never from a `wl-*` ref-name pattern — and
  the residual risk (a worktree-backed fixture branch) is documented in the module docstring.
- **AC7** F2's sandbox + snapshot contract tests are green. *Verification:*
  `pytest skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`.

- **Covers parent **AC1 — Hermetic git usage:** every test helper that runs real `git` commands


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (new) — sandbox factories, snapshot/compare, worktree registration exclusion.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_skill_extensions.py`

## Summary

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out (many concurrent `audit_runner.py issue OSL-*` processes) ran the test suite with a **leaked `GIT_DIR`** pointing at a live worktree's git dir. Tests that use real `git` (git init/commit/push fixtures) therefore operated on the **live repository** instead of their temp dirs: they committed 24 junk commits (`init`/`Initial commit`, authors `Test <test@test.com>`, `T <t@t>`, `Cache Test`, `RT Test`) on top of the then-current `dev` tip and **pushed them to `origin/dev`**, gutting the branch (483 files, -144,702 lines).

This is the exact incident class documented in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (2026-09-24 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident, SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 / docs/dev/test-isolation.md) — the sandbox helper neutralises the vars for test fixtures, but the **production test-execution path does not**.

## Evidence

- Orphaned (`PPID 1`) `audit_runner.py issue OSL-*` processes with env:
  `GIT_DIR=/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.git/worktrees/wl-OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT-nested-node-modules`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core`, `GIT_PREFIX=`.
- Their `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings` children inherited the same `GIT_DIR`.
- `refs/heads/dev` reflog: last legitimate entry `763b8f11` (push by Sorra the Orc), then 24 test commits by `T/Test/Cache Test/RT Test`.
- `refs/heads/dev` and the shared `.git/config` (`core.bare=true`) were rewritten; `.git/HEAD` moved to junk.
- `git ls-remote origin dev` showed the junk tip `6366f913` (fast-forward from `763b8f11`, so the push was accepted).

## Impact

- `origin/dev` overwritten (recovered to `763b8f11` via `--force-with-lease` by the implement session).
- Shared main checkout `core.bare=true`, `dev` ref clobbered (recovered).
- Collateral: another agent's uncommitted work in the main checkout was reset/lost.
- Any push/CI consuming `dev` during the window would have seen the gutted tree.

## Root cause / propagation

- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner` does `env = os.environ.copy()` and passes it to `subprocess.run` **without stripping `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`**. `GIT_DIR` overrides `cwd` for every git subprocess, so fixture `git init/commit/push` hit the live repo.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_run_tests_via_test_skill` -> `run_cached`) have the same gap.
- The origin of the leaked `GIT_DIR` in the launcher is external to `skill/` (no setter found in the repo); the audit fan-out was orphaned. **Defence-in-depth must not depend on the launcher being clean.**

## Proposed fix

1. Scrub `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` (from `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`) in `test_cache._default_runner` (and any other subprocess that runs tests) before spawning — single choke point.
2. `run_tests.py`: strip the same vars in its runner/env.
3. `audit_runner.py`: strip before `run_cached`/`run_tests`; ensure per-item audits cannot fan out unbounded (34+ concurrent observed).
4. Regression test: with `GIT_DIR` set to the live repo in `os.environ`, a fixture `git init/commit` must NOT touch  the live checkout (extend `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`).
5. Consider making the live-repo guard fail-fast (abort the run) rather than only post-hoc, and have `run_tests.py` refuse to run when `GIT_DIR`/override vars are present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test_cache._default_runner` (and `run_tests.py`/`audit_runner.py`) remove `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_CONFIG*`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` before spawning tests.
- [ ] Regression test reproduces the leak (fixture mutation under a poisoned `GIT_DIR`) and proves the scrub prevents it.
- [ ] `origin/dev` cannot be moved by any test fixture (asserted).
- [ ] Audit fan-out is bounded (`AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS` honoured; no 30+ concurrent orphans).
- [ ] Full suite green.
