# live-repo mutation guard false-positives when the suite runs inside an agent worktree

`discovered-from:SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`

## Problem statement

When the full test suite runs **inside an agent worktree** (the normal `implement.py finish` and `/skill:test` case), the live-repo mutation guard anchors its agent-worktree exclusion on the *passed root* rather than the **main checkout**. Inside a linked worktree that root is the worktree itself, so `excluded_refs` is always empty and any concurrent agent committing to another worktree is reported as a mutation — failing the run and blocking the full-suite release gate for every agent whenever the shared host has more than one active session.

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents running `/skill:test` or `implement.py finish` from inside an `implement` worktree on a shared multi-agent host.
- **Secondary:** the human producer relying on the full-suite exit code as the pre-push release gate.
- **Tertiary:** maintainers of the shared `git_sandbox.py` helper and the two guards that consume it.

Example user stories:

- As an **implementing agent**, I want the full suite to run green inside my worktree even while sibling agents commit to theirs, so that concurrent sessions do not block my release gate.
- As a **producer**, I want the guard to keep failing on genuine in-place mutation of the guarded checkout, so that real corruption (the `GIT_DIR` incident, SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) is never reported as green.
- As a **maintainer**, I want one shared fix in `git_sandbox.py`, so the outer `run_tests.py` guard and the inner `live_repo_guard.py` conftest guard cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `snapshot_repo_state()` called with a **linked-worktree root** returns `excluded_refs` containing every branch checked out in a registered worktree under the **main checkout's** `.worklog/worktrees/` (not `<passed_root>/.worklog/worktrees`). Verification: a unit test creates a main repo plus an agent worktree, calls `snapshot_repo_state(worktree_root)`, and asserts the agent worktree's `refs/heads/wl-*` is in `excluded_refs`.
- [ ] **No false positive:** with the guard/snapshot armed at a linked-worktree root, advancing a branch checked out in a *sibling* agent worktree produces `diff_snapshots(before, after)["changed"] == False` and does not fail the guard. Verification: a nested-pytest test that arms the guard inside a worktree, commits in a sibling worktree, and asserts exit code 0 with no `live-repo mutation` text (red on the pre-fix helper).
- [ ] **No false negative:** an in-place mutation of the guarded checkout is still reported — (a) moving `HEAD`/the guarded branch ref, (b) modifying a tracked file, (c) adding an untracked non-ignored file. Verification: the existing `TestSnapshotContract` cases still pass when the guard is armed at a worktree root.
- [ ] **Worktree registration churn does not fail:** registering or removing a worktree under `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` during a guarded run does not fail the guard when the reportable diff is empty. Verification: a unit test where `excluded_refs` grows but `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == False` asserts the per-test guard does not fail.
- [ ] **Single shared fix:** both the `run_tests.py` outer guard (`_detect_live_repo_mutation`) and the conftest inner guard (`live_repo_guard.py`) exhibit the corrected behaviour, with the anchoring logic living only in `git_sandbox.py`. Verification: code review plus the guard-level nested-pytest tests.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the reported failure (red against the pre-fix helper) and passes after the fix, covering the `wl-SA-0MUD5R5EQ...-fix-inherited-pass...` worktree scenario and the observed `moved ref refs/heads/wl-*` suite failures.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. This includes the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring's exclusion-derivation note and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` must remain **stdlib-only** and loadable by file location — the repo-root `conftest.py` loads it via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and must not mutate `sys.path`.
- Agent-worktree exclusion must be **derived from git plumbing** (e.g. `git worktree list --porcelain`, or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to locate the main checkout) — **never** a `wl-*` name pattern. The module docstring documents why: a name pattern would also exclude the incident's own fixture branches and destroy detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX class of bug.
- Snapshots stay **read-only**: only plumbing commands; never `gc`, `update-index`, `fetch`, or `--refresh`.
- The fix must not weaken genuine mutation detection (moved `dev`, config rewrites, tracked/untracked file changes).
- Any extra git invocation per snapshot must be cheap and confined to the snapshot path; it must not turn the per-test fingerprint into a full `status` scan.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_parse_worktrees` computes `agent_root = root.joinpath(*AGENT_WORKTREE_DIR)`, where `root` is the passed root (for `snapshot_repo_state`, the `git_toplevel(resolved)` of the passed path).
- Reproduced 2026-09-26 on `dev @ 10995367`:
  - `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from the **main checkout** → `excluded_refs` contains all 12 agent-worktree branches.
  - `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSRN0Q64005YR5A-stale-pytest-exit` → `git_toplevel` is the worktree root and `excluded_refs == set()`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` arms with `root` from `_default_root(config)` (or the repo-root conftest's `_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent`, which inside a worktree is the worktree root).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_detect_live_repo_mutation` calls `snapshot_repo_state(project_root)` where `project_root` comes from `detect_project_root()` (worktree root when run inside one). It shares the same helper and the same defect.
- Adjacent defect (same guard path, reproduced): `fingerprint()` includes `tuple(sorted(excluded))`, and `pytest_runtest_teardown` fails whenever the fingerprint differs — regardless of `diff_snapshots(...)["changed"]`. Adding a second worktree under `.worklog/worktrees/` mid-run changes `excluded` while the diff stays clean, so worktree registration churn is a second false positive.
- Existing tests only arm the guard at the **main** root (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestLiveRepoGuard::test_agent_worktree_churn_does_not_trip_the_guard` creates the worktree under the root it arms), so they do not exercise the linked-worktree case.

Minimal reproduction (from any linked worktree):

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents")
from skill.shared import git_sandbox as gs
snap = gs.snapshot_repo_state(".")
print(snap["root"], len(snap["worktrees"]), snap["excluded_refs"])
PY
# from a worktree: excluded_refs == set()  (bug)
# from the main checkout: excluded_refs has every agent-worktree branch
```

## Desired change

- Add a small helper that resolves the **main checkout root** from git plumbing (first entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`, or the parent of `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), and anchor agent-worktree exclusion on `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` rather than the passed root.
- Thread that anchor through `_parse_worktrees` / `snapshot_repo_state`. When the passed root *is* the main checkout the behaviour is unchanged; when it is a linked worktree the exclusion set is now populated correctly.
- Make the per-test guard fail only when `diff_snapshots` reports a reportable change (or exclude the `excluded`-set churn from the fingerprint), so worktree registration/deregistration is not a false positive while the authoritative full diff still catches real mutations.
- Add regression tests at both levels (helper and guard) and document the main-checkout anchoring in the module docstring and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — Add a main-checkout resolver and change `_parse_worktrees`/`snapshot_repo_state` to anchor `agent_root` on `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/`; address `fingerprint()`/`diff_snapshots` treatment of the excluded set. Module docstring's exclusion-derivation note needs updating.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — `pytest_runtest_teardown` must fail only when the authoritative diff is non-empty (not merely when the cheap fingerprint moves); affects `__init__`, `pytest_runtest_teardown`, `pytest_sessionfinish`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — Add `snapshot_repo_state(worktree_root)` exclusion test, sibling-churn no-false-positive test, in-place mutation still-reported test, and excluded-set-churn test (class `TestAgentWorktreeExclusion`).
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` — Add a nested-pytest test that arms the guard from inside a linked worktree and commits in a sibling worktree (exit 0, no `live-repo mutation` text); keep the existing main-root test.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Verify `_detect_live_repo_mutation` benefits from the shared fix; add a focused test if the outer guard needs its own coverage.
- `conftest.py` — Confirm the repo-root conftest continues to arm the guard correctly from a worktree (helper-side fix preferred over conftest change).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — Document main-checkout anchoring and the two false-positive classes.
- `skill/shared/tests/` / `tests/` — New regression tests; `tests/fixtures/` or helper fixtures if a nested-worktree harness is needed.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the operator intends the anchor fix (AC1–AC3, AC5) as the core scope; the worktree-registration churn (AC4) is included because it is the same guard code path and the same symptom class. If the producer prefers, AC4 can be split into a follow-up work item — recorded here rather than silently dropped.
- **Risk (implementation):** relying on `git worktree list --porcelain` ordering (main worktree first) is documented git behaviour but somewhat implicit; prefer `--git-common-dir` or validate the first entry to avoid a fragile assumption.
- **Risk (regression / security):** an incorrect anchor could over- or under-exclude and either mask the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX incident or keep the false positive. Mitigated by AC3 (no false negative) and the existing contract tests.
- **Risk (scope creep):** expanding into a general refactor of the guard. Recorded mitigation: keep changes surgical to the anchoring + fingerprint decision and link any extra opportunity as a separate work item.
- **Risk (performance):** the extra main-root resolution must be cached per snapshot so the per-test fingerprint stays cheap.
- **Risk (test flakiness):** the nested-pytest tests must remain hermetic under `tmp_path` (use the existing `git_sandbox` factories, never the live checkout).

## Related work

- `SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ` — repo-root conftest live-repo guard (introduced the inner guard).
- `SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H` — `run_tests.py` live-repo snapshot guard (the outer guard that shares the helper).
- `SA-0MUG30IIR00978CW` — hermetic git sandbox helper and migration (owns `git_sandbox.py`).
- `SA-0MUG30HV8004HV94` — guard contract tests and guard-fires proof.
- `SA-0MUG30KEV006RBAM` — document hermetic-git requirement and guard.
- `SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS` — live-repo guard teardown ordering (adjacent `live_repo_guard.py` defect; shows the same test file is the home for guard regressions).
- `SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q` — `implement.py run_tests` bypasses `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` (adjacent guard-activation defect; not blocking, but touching the same guard read-path).
- `SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` — leaked `GIT_DIR` incident (the guard's reason to exist; must stay detected).
- `SA-0MU89WA740004GOJ` — destructive `init` commit wiped repo on `dev` (test-isolation incident context).
- `SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF` — multi-agent audit/test coordination (the contention context that makes this reproducible).
- `SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0` — audit-runner pre-review bypass (source item; `discovered-from`).
- `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` — remote `dev` corruption / test isolation (origin of `git_sandbox.py` and the snapshot design).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — incident write-up and guarded-worktree proof; documents the snapshot/exclusion contract.
- `docs/dev/repro_live_repo_leak.py` — reproduction harness for the leak class the guard protects.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed context (`discovered-from:SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`) already contained the problem, root-cause pointer, expected behaviour, measurable ACs, and related work, and the defect was reproduced directly during intake. Questions below were resolved by repo investigation and recorded for auditability.

- Q: "Is `excluded_refs` really empty when the guard runs inside a linked worktree?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSRN0Q64005YR5A-stale-pytest-exit` returned `excluded_refs == set()`, while the same call from the main checkout returned 12 agent-worktree refs. Evidence: `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_parse_worktrees` (`agent_root = root.joinpath(*AGENT_WORKTREE_DIR)`) and the 2026-09-26 reproduction on `dev @ 10995367`.
- Q: "Does `run_tests.py`'s outer guard share the same defect?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `_detect_live_repo_mutation` calls `snapshot_repo_state(project_root)` and `diff_snapshots`, both from the shared helper; the conftest guard does the same. Evidence: `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`, `conftest.py`.
- Q: "Is there an adjacent false positive from concurrent worktree registration/deregistration?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `fingerprint()` includes `tuple(sorted(excluded))` and `pytest_runtest_teardown` fails on any fingerprint change, so registering a second worktree mid-run fails the guard even though `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == False`. Reproduced with a temp repo: adding `wl-two` changed the fingerprint while the diff stayed clean. Assumed in scope (AC4) as the same guard path; flagged for producer confirmation.
- Q: "Should the fix change the root the conftest/`run_tests.py` pass in, or the helper?" — Answer (agent, decision): the **helper** (`git_sandbox.py`) so both guards benefit and cannot drift (AC5). The passed root may legitimately be a worktree; the helper must resolve the main checkout itself.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)
- **SA-0MRNW4BN70084S84** – [test-failure] test_other_stages_ask_only_when_genuinely_unclear — failing test (completed)

## Failure Signature

- Test name: skill/shared/tests/test_queue.py::test_remove_takes_specific_item_only
- Failing commit: 1590f4707b40017f0f0efff7f6dc69da6d7c653a
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
live-repo mutation detected during skill/shared/tests/test_queue.py::test_remove_takes_specific_item_only:
  (no differences)
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 1590f4707b40017f0f0efff7f6dc69da6d7c653a`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k skill/shared/tests/test_queue.py::test_remove_takes_specific_item_only` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Root Cause Analysis (added by plan)

The failure is a **false positive in the live-repo mutation guard**, not a defect in `test_remove_takes_specific_item_only` (the test passes in isolation on `dev @ edfbdfcd`). The `"(no differences)"` text is the tell-tale: the guard decided the checkout had mutated but could not render a single reportable change.

`skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py::pytest_runtest_teardown` fails a test when the **cheap fingerprint** changes:

- `LiveRepoMutationGuard` stores `self._baseline = fingerprint(snapshot_repo_state(root, include_status=False))` at session start.
- On teardown it compares `fingerprint(...)` again and `pytest.fail`s when they differ, rendering the failure with `describe_diff(diff_snapshots(self.before, current))`.

`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::fingerprint` returns `(refs-minus-excluded, config, sorted(excluded_refs))`, but `diff_snapshots` **filters `excluded_refs` out of both sides** and never puts them in a diff category. Therefore a change **only in the `excluded_refs` set** changes the fingerprint (guard fails) while `describe_diff` has nothing to print → `"(no differences)"`.

`excluded_refs` is derived from `git worktree list --porcelain` for branches checked out under `<checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/`. On this shared multi-agent host, `implement.py start`/`finish` register and remove agent worktrees continuously, so the excluded set churns mid-run and trips the per-test guard against whichever test happens to be running — `test_remove_takes_specific_item_only` here.

Reproduced deterministically against the two helpers (same inputs, one worktree registration):

```
fingerprint differs: True
diff changed: False
describe:   (no differences)
```

Related triage-bot evidence on this item shows the same class of churn with a non-empty diff (`deleted ref refs/heads/wl-SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ-...` + `deleted config branch.wl-...`), confirming concurrent agent-worktree registration/removal is the trigger.

## Relationship / Duplicate Assessment

- **Covered by (blocker):** SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 — *live-repo guard false-positives inside an agent worktree (concurrent worktree ref churn)* (`in-progress`, Small/High). Its AC *"Worktree registration churn does not fail: registering or removing a worktree under `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` during a guarded run does not fail the guard when the reportable diff is empty"* is exactly this signature, and it explicitly requires the shared fix to live in `git_sandbox.py` so the inner and outer guards cannot drift. Fixing this item separately would edit the same helper concurrently and produce conflicting changes.
- **Related:** SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH — *Live-repo guard: shared refs/stash causes spurious mutation failures across concurrent worktrees* (shared-ref churn; different surface, same "spurious guard failure" family).
- **Decision:** do **not** decompose or implement this item independently. It is a verification/triage artefact of SA-0MUILGH5E007X627; this item should be closed once that fix lands and the test stays green under concurrent worktree churn.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `skill/shared/tests/test_queue.py::test_remove_takes_specific_item_only` passes when run against the latest `dev`, including under concurrent agent-worktree registration/removal churn (the guard no longer emits `"(no differences)"` for excluded-ref churn).
2. The root cause is covered by a regression test in `skill/shared/tests/` where `excluded_refs` grows but `diff_snapshots(before, after)["changed"] == False`, and the per-test guard does **not** fail (delivered by SA-0MUILGH5E007X627); genuine mutations (moved branch/ref, tracked/untracked file change, config rewrite) are still reported.
3. Documentation describing the exclusion/`fingerprint` contract is updated to state that `excluded_refs` churn alone must never fail the guard (`git_sandbox.py` docstrings and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`).
4. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `fingerprint()` / `diff_snapshots()` consistency for `excluded_refs`
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — per-test guard consumer of `fingerprint()`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — regression tests for snapshot/fingerprint/diff contracts
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — guard/exclusion documentation

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

No blocking questions were required. Assessment was evidence-driven from the repository and existing work items:

- Where does `"(no differences)"` originate? Answer (plan, code): `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::describe_diff` when `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == True` but lists no entries; combined with `live_repo_guard.py`'s fingerprint check this isolates the `excluded_refs`-only change. No question needed for the producer.
- Is this already covered elsewhere? Answer (plan, worklog search): SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 has an AC for registration churn with an empty reportable diff; SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH covers shared-ref churn. Recorded as a blocking relationship above.

## Summary

Test-first regression coverage proving that a poisoned repository-override environment cannot reach the live checkout through the production test-execution paths. This is the tracer bullet for the whole work item: the tests must FAIL against the current code and PASS once the scrub (F2/F3) lands.

**Target outcome:** a fixture that sets `GIT_DIR` (and the other `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`) to a throwaway *victim* repository, then drives each production test-execution entry point, can prove the victim repo is byte-for-byte unmoved.

**Definition of done:** pytest tests exist that (a) reproduce the leak against pre-fix code, (b) pass once the scrub is wired in, and (c) assert `origin/dev` cannot be moved by a fixture.

**Constraints:** stdlib + pytest only; no network; must not touch the real checkout — use a `tmp_path` victim repo and `snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`.

**Risky assumptions:** that the production paths can be driven in-process without executing the full suite. Where not possible, use a minimal sentinel command via the runner protocol.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `GIT_DIR` set to a throwaway victim repo in the process env, invoking `test_cache._default_runner(command, cwd, timeout)` for a command that runs `git init`/`git commit` leaves the victim repo's refs and local config unchanged (pre-fix: changed).
- [ ] With the same poisoned env, `run_tests._cached_runner` / `_run_cmd` leaves the victim repo's refs and local config unchanged.
- [ ] With the same poisoned env, `audit_runner._run_tests_via_test_skill` does not propagate the override vars into the suite subprocess (asserted on the subprocess env).
- [ ] The regression tests fail against pre-fix code (verified by temporarily reverting the scrub or by asserting the pre-fix helper is also covered).
- [ ] A test asserts that no fixture can move `refs/heads/dev` / `origin/dev` in the live checkout (victim-repo proxy assertion).

- [ ] Parent AC traceability: the regression test reproduces the leak (fixture mutation under a poisoned `GIT_DIR`) and proves the scrub prevents it.
**Key Files:**
- skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py
- skill/shared/git_sandbox.py
- tests/test_test_cache.py
- tests/test_run_tests_cache.py
- skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py

**Dependencies:** none (first item).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli
- Failing commit: 0d0d0fc0ab144e796ce616d8f5436e6a70dd4bed
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
live-repo mutation detected during tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli:
  added config   branch.wl-SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99-r1-audit-debug-log-mislabels-every-succe.merge=refs/heads/dev
  added config   branch.wl-SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99-r1-audit-debug-log-mislabels-every-succe.remote=.
```

## Root Cause (evidence-backed)

The named test is **not defective** — it is the *victim* of a false positive in
the live-repo mutation guard (F5, SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ). The guard fails whichever
test finishes next when the main checkout's shared `.git/config` changes mid-run:

- `implement.py::git_worktree_add()` runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> dev`,
  which writes `branch.<branch>.remote=.` and `branch.<branch>.merge=refs/heads/dev`
  into the **main checkout's shared `.git/config`**.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::snapshot_repo_state()` captures **all** local config
  (`git config --local --list`).
- `fingerprint()` (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py:414`) and `diff_snapshots()`
  (`:446-455`) filter agent-worktree **refs** via `excluded_refs`, but do **not**
  filter the matching `branch.<excluded-ref>.{remote,merge}` config keys.
- `live_repo_guard.py::pytest_runtest_teardown` therefore sees a config diff caused
  by a concurrent agent's `implement.py start` and fails the next test to finish —
  here the ~6.7 s cleanup integration test.

This is the same guard false-positive class as SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 (worktree-root
anchoring / ref churn) and SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH (shared `refs/stash` churn), and
reproduces the root cause first identified for SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91 (closed as a
false positive without a guard fix).

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 0d0d0fc0ab144e796ce616d8f5436e6a70dd4bed`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item. Because the guard misattributes a concurrent
worktree's config churn to an unrelated test, the failure is non-deterministic and
will recur on any shared host with more than one active agent session.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. The live-repo mutation guard no longer reports a mutation for `branch.<worktree-branch>.remote` / `.merge` config churn written by a concurrent `implement.py start` / worktree registration. Verification: a test mutates the shared `.git/config` branch keys for a branch present in `excluded_refs` and asserts `diff_snapshots(before, after)["changed"] is False` and `fingerprint()` is unchanged.
3. Genuine in-place checkout mutations are still reported (moved `HEAD`/branch ref, tracked-file edit, untracked non-ignored file, unrelated config change); the existing guard contract tests remain green.
4. Documentation describing the guard's exclusion surface (e.g. `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` and the `git_sandbox.py` docstring) is updated to state that worktree-branch config keys are excluded.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MUILGH5E007X627** — live-repo guard false-positives inside an agent worktree (concurrent worktree ref churn) (open)
- **SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH** — Live-repo guard: shared refs/stash causes spurious mutation failures across concurrent worktrees (open)
- **SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91** — same failure signature; closed as a false positive without a guard fix (completed)

## Key Files:

- `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py`
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`
- `scripts/cleanup/prune_local_branches.py`
- `scripts/cleanup/cleanup_stale_remote_branches.py`
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Plan skill auto-skip path (effort Extra Small, risk Low): no interactive interview was
run. Questions arising from automated review are recorded below.

- **OPEN QUESTION** (directed to: producer / Build): the guard false-positive class already
  has two open items (SA-0MUILGH5E007X627, SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH). Should the `branch.<ref>.*`
  config-key filter be implemented here (as AC2 implies), or folded into SA-0MUILGH5E007X627
  as the single shared `git_sandbox.py` fix — with this item then closed as a duplicate symptom?
  Why it matters: proceeding here without a decision risks two divergent fixes to the same helper.
  Recommendation: fold into SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 and close this item as a duplicate, unless the
  producer prefers this item to carry the regression test.
- **Q:** Is the named test itself in scope for change? **Answer (plan review):** no. The test is
  valid; it is only the guard's attribution that is wrong. Evidence: the previous root-cause
  analysis for SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91 and the reproduction above.

# Migrate remaining raw-git test helpers to `skill/shared/git_sandbox`

**discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents)

## Context

SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 closed the audit-identified AC1 gap by routing the residual
raw `git` invocations in `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` and
`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` through the shared sandbox
(`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`). A repo-wide sweep during that work found the
same non-hermetic pattern in further test helpers: these shell out to
`subprocess.run(["git", ...], cwd=...)` and therefore inherit any leaked
repository-overriding environment variable (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`,
`GIT_CONFIG*`), exactly the incident mechanism (SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 parent AC1:
"every test helper that runs real `git` commands … carries `GIT_DIR`/
`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_CONFIG_*`/identity isolation where needed").

The F5 live-repo guard (`skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` + repo-root
`conftest.py`) detects and fails a run if the live checkout is mutated, so this
is defence-in-depth rather than an unguarded hole — but the helpers themselves
are still non-hermetic.

## Remaining raw-git call sites (count as of 2026-09-26)

| File | Raw git calls |
|------|---------------|
| `tests/test_status_lifecycle.py` | 6 |
| `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py` | 6 |
| `tests/test_implement_worktree_enforcement.py` | 6 |
| `tests/test_implement_submodules.py` | 6 |
| `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` | 6 |
| `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py` | 6 |
| `tests/test_implement_code_freeze_gate.py` | 5 |
| `tests/test_wl_sync_no_commits.py` | 4 |
| `tests/test_test_cache.py` | 1 (local `_git()` wrapper) |
| `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` | 1 (local `_git()` wrapper) |
| `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py` | 1 (local `_git()` wrapper) |
| `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` | 1 |
| `tests/test_refactor/test_session_boundary.py` | 1 (commented example) |
| `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` | 1 (git helper) |

Typical pattern (the `isolated_git_repo` fixtures):

```python
subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=str(repo_root), check=True, capture_output=True)
subprocess.run(["git", "config", "user.email", "test@test.com"], cwd=..., check=True, ...)
subprocess.run(["git", "config", "user.name", "Test"], cwd=..., check=True, ...)
subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=..., check=True, ...)
subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", "Initial commit"], cwd=..., check=True, ...)
subprocess.run(["git", "branch", "dev"], cwd=..., check=True, ...)
subprocess.run(["git", "worktree", "add", "--track", "-b", ...], cwd=..., check=True, ...)
```

## Desired change

Route every remaining real-git invocation in test helpers through
`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (`init_repo`, `commit_all`, `add_worktree`,
`add_remote`, `run_git`), so that:

- the repository-overriding environment variables are neutralised;
- fixture identity is injected (`-c user.name=… -c user.email=…`) rather than
  written into a repo-local config;
- the fixture repository is asserted to sit under `tmp_path` (containment).

audit blocker — environment over-dispatch + infra-fallback state corruption (blocked; producer input needed)

## What happened

I ran the audit runner for this item. The host is currently over-dispatched: ~9 concurrent `audit_runner.py` processes share the local model backend, which has **only 1 slot** (`/llama/local/status`: `total_slots: 1`, `available_slots: 0`) and system load average ~60 on 16 cores. The runner's host-wide `audit` semaphore (`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`) and the proxy's single slot starve individual audit calls.

Initially the runner was further handicapped: the proxy reported `cheap` mode at launch, which forces `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`; combined with `Semaphore._try_acquire_slot()` only iterating `range(max_workers)`, the run could only use flock slot 0 and hit `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` (90s) repeatedly ("Audit concurrency limit reached"). Pinning `--max-concurrency 5` (CLI precedence) fixed the slot-index starvation, but the single local-model slot remains the binding constraint, so calls still stall at the 600s in-process guard.

## State corruption (repaired) — needs confirmation

During an early `--audit-children` run (aborted mid-cascade), the auto-triggered child audits persisted **infra-fallback `No`** reports and demoted the three children from `completed`/`in_review` to `open`/`blocked` + `plan_complete`. Their reports are entirely fallback-tainted, e.g.

> `partial` — "Pi model output could not be parsed … Audit concurrency limit reached: audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated: no slot within 90s … Phase: Phase 1 child screening (SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ)."

Per the audit skill, an infra-fallback `No` is *not* an explicit model assessment and must **restore** the pre-audit state, not demote. I therefore restored the three children to `completed`/`in_review`:

- SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ
- SA-0MUDD7BHE006V3RI
- SA-0MUDUW8CI008B73L

Their stored audits are still the fallback `No` reports (there is no `wl` audit-clear primitive), so a future audit without `--force` could reuse them. They should be overwritten by a proper `--force` re-audit, or explicitly invalidated.

The item itself is left `blocked`/`in_review` (a non-terminal child exists, see below); this is the resting state.

## Spurious blocking child (needs producer decision)

Running the audit auto-executed the repo suite, which is **red for environmental reasons, not code reasons**:

- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` asserts host-wide semaphore limits; the concurrent audits violate those assertions (`assert 5 <= 2`, `assert 4 <= 1`, `assert 3 == 1`).
- `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` fails the **live-repo guard** because an unrelated concurrent agent added `branch.wl-SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99-….merge=refs/heads/dev` to the shared repo git config during the test.
- pytest also collects duplicate tests from `.worklog/worktrees/**` (paths like `…/skill/skill/shared/tests/…`).

The test skill's triage created **SA-0MUIVIHHT009K3VS** (`[test-failure] tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli`) as a **child of this item** (heuristic `commit_or_ci_url`), which now blocks this item's closure even though the failure is environment-induced and unrelated to the eslint fix.

## Substantive result (fix verified)

The eslint `.py`-target fix itself is confirmed by Phase 1 with file:line evidence, all three parent ACs `met`:

1. Scoped eslint filters to JS/TS — `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py:91` (`ESLINT_EXTENSIONS`), `:363-376` (`_run_eslint_findings_check`), `:748-765` (`_run_eslint_fix_mode`).

3. `.py`-only scope completes without an eslint parsing-error blocker — evidence chain via `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:8800-8803` → `run_linters_for_project` → `run_eslint(files=…)`.

The audit's code-quality scan produced **no blocking findings** (the pipeline proceeded past Phase 1 step 1), i.e. the false high-severity eslint findings no longer occur.

## Questions for the producer

1. Confirm the restoration of the three children to `completed`/`in_review` is correct, and how the fallback-tainted `No` audits should be invalidated (or authorise a `--force` re-audit once the host is free).
2. How should the environment-induced, mis-parented child **SA-0MUIVIHHT009K3VS** be handled — close as spurious, re-parent to the responsible item (SA-0MUIMLPLH006TKY1 owns the sibling triage item), or leave it blocking?
3. Should audit dispatch be throttled (serially, or with a raised `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` / `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT`) given the single-slot local model, to prevent concurrency-limit fallbacks and their state side-effects?

Per producer answers: closed the false-positive child `SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91`, restored the five original children to `completed`/`in_review`, and attempted the audit re-run.

**First re-run attempt (aborted 22:38 UTC).** `--force --no-child-in-main-slot` with the slot-aware status URL. Aborted before persistence to avoid overwriting the stored audit.

**Second re-run attempt (aborted 23:17 UTC).** Relaunched with `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT=7200` (the same workaround a peer audit is using) so calls wait for the slot instead of failing fast. The full suite timed out after 1500 s (0 failures triaged, so no new children), the merge gate passed, and the audit slot was acquired immediately (`wait_seconds=0.00`). However, the parent Phase 1 `pi` call then **stalled for >9 minutes with ~1 s of CPU** because the Local Proxy has **0 of 3 slots free** — it is saturated by many long-running agent sessions (several `pi` processes running 1–1.5 h). Aborted before the 600 s stall-timeout cascade (≈6 calls × 10 min) could persist another fallback-tainted verdict.

**Conclusion:** the bottleneck is Local Proxy *capacity*, not the audit admission queue. A clean Local Proxy audit is not achievable while the proxy is saturated, regardless of `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`.

**Current state:** item restored to `completed`/`in_review`; children all terminal; the stored audit remains the 18:16:20 fallback-tainted "Ready to close: No" (unchanged, not overwritten). No code changes were made.

**Question for the producer:**

Either retry later when the Local Proxy is genuinely idle (0 free slots now), or run the audit on the remote model (`--model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --model-source remote`), which bypasses Local Proxy contention entirely — a concurrent runner is already using it successfully. Implementation complete — producer authorised option B (Q1: approve blocker plan as-is; Q2: keep AC4 in scope).

## Changes (shared guard fix)

All functional changes live in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` and `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` so the two guard consumers cannot drift:

1. `fingerprint()` no longer folds `tuple(sorted(excluded_refs))` in, and filters the `branch.<excluded>.{remote,merge}` config that `git worktree add --track` writes.
2. `diff_snapshots()` filters that same excluded-branch config, using the union of both snapshots excluded sets so a worktree appearing/disappearing mid-run is invisible on either side.
3. `main_checkout_root()` anchors agent-worktree exclusion on the **main checkout** via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (parent when named `.git`), fallback = first `git worktree list --porcelain` entry — never a `wl-*` pattern. `snapshot_repo_state()` threads it into `_parse_worktrees`. This fixes the linked-worktree case (`implement.py finish` runs the suite from a worktree; previously `excluded_refs` was empty there).
4. `pytest_runtest_teardown()` treats the cheap fingerprint as a **trigger only**: it consults the authoritative `diff_snapshots(...)` and returns (re-baselining) when `changed == False`, so excluded-set churn can no longer fail a clean test with `(no differences)`. `self.offender` is now set only on a genuine mutation.

## Tests (all verified RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix)

- helper-level: `TestAgentWorktreeChurn` + `TestMainCheckoutAnchoring` in `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` (registration no-track, `--track` config churn, removal-with-retained-branch, existing-branch-becomes-excluded, linked-worktree anchoring, non-excluded config rewrite still reported);
- guard-level: registration / `--track` registration / removal / linked-worktree sibling churn do-not-fire, plus config-rewrite fires, in `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`.

## Docs

`git_sandbox.py` module/constant docstrings and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 (exclusion contract, main-checkout anchoring, no-false-positive/no-false-negative guarantees).

- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`: 12 passed.

Plan (auto-skip path) — effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low** (below threshold), plus a producer handoff.

## Root cause (evidence-backed, deterministically reproduced)

The named test is **not defective**. It passes at the recorded failing commit `e2218e77` *and* at current `dev` `ba9f2dd5`. The failure is a **false positive in the live-repo mutation guard** caused by a *concurrent* agent on this shared host:

- `SA-0MUFSIB1U0088YEB` ran `implement.py start` at 17:54:43Z and pushed at 18:23:54Z — overlapping this item's run (created 18:01:21Z).
- `implement.py::git_worktree_add()` runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> dev`, which writes `branch.<branch>.remote=.` and `branch.<branch>.merge=refs/heads/dev` into the **main checkout's shared `.git/config`**.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::snapshot_repo_state()` captures **all** local config. `fingerprint()` / `diff_snapshots()` filter agent-worktree **refs** via `excluded_refs`, but do **not** filter the matching `branch.<excluded-ref>.*` **config** keys.
- `live_repo_guard.py::pytest_runtest_teardown` therefore sees a genuine (non-empty) config diff and fails whichever test finishes next — here `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` (6.7 s subprocess test). The triage helper then attached the first failing pytest node id, which is how this item got its (unrelated) title.

Hermetic reproduction with the shared helper:

```
excluded_refs after: ['refs/heads/wl-TEST-config-churn']
fingerprint changed: True
diff changed: True
config added:
    branch.wl-TEST-config-churn.remote = .
    branch.wl-TEST-config-churn.merge = refs/heads/dev
```

This matches the triage evidence verbatim (`added config branch.wl-SA-0MUFSIB1U0088YEB-...remote/.merge`).

## Verification — every test named in the triage evidence passes on current `dev` `ba9f2dd5`

- `skill/audit/tests/test_persist_audit_priority.py::TestBestEffortPriorityAdjustment::test_priority_fetch_failure_still_persists` — passed (also passes at `e2218e77`)
- `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` — passed

- `tests/test_audit_runner_review.py::TestCmdIssueJsonMode::test_default_mode_still_emits_markdown` — passed

## Review stages (auto-complete path)

1. **Finished Requirements & AC alignment review:** AC1 ("test passes on latest dev") is already satisfied; the ACs do not describe the real defect (guard config surface). Intent not rewritten.
2. **Finished Completeness review:** description lacked root-cause evidence and Key Files; no `**Key Files:**` section existed to validate. RCA recorded above.
3. **Finished Sequencing & dependencies review:** no children; the coherent sequencing is a blocking edge to the guard fix.
4. **Finished Scope sizing review:** no children; item confirmed Extra Small.
5. **Finished Acceptance & testability review:** ACs are pass/fail; AC1 verified true. AC2 (docs) is a no-op without a code change; AC3 not re-run here.
6. **Finished Polish & handoff review:** description augmented with actionable RCA and pointers for the guard owner.

AC coverage review (`skill.shared.tree_coverage.run_coverage_review`): `recommendation: proceed` — no children, no conflicts, parent ACs fully covered.

## Related / duplicate assessment

- `SA-0MUILGH5E007X627` (open, intake_complete) — worktree **ref** churn when the suite runs inside a worktree. Its ACs cover registration churn only **when the reportable diff is empty**, and explicitly require config rewrites to stay detected. It does **not** cover this config-surface variant.
- `SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH` (open, idea) — shared refs/stash churn; same spurious-guard-failure family.
- `SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65` (blocked, plan_complete) — sibling triage item with the same "named test passes, guard false positive" pattern; dispositioned by blocking on `SA-0MUILGH5E007X627`.
- `SA-0MUF9TXFN009I6Q2` (completed) and `SA-0MUGXZGVZ001UFPG` (completed) — separately triaged instances of the `test_run_tests_scope.py` evidence attached here.
- No existing item covers excluding `branch.<excluded-ref>.{remote,merge}` config from the guarded surface.

## OPEN QUESTIONS (producer input required)

- **OPEN QUESTION Q1 — Disposition of this item.** The premise (a failing test) is false and AC1 is already met, so there is nothing to implement here. Options: (a) block this item on the guard fix and close it once the guard change lands (mirrors `SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65`); (b) close now as a false positive with a `discovered-from` pointer; (c) implement the guard fix here. **Recommended: (a)** — keeps the test-failure item accountable to the guard fix without duplicating it.
- **OPEN QUESTION Q2 — Where should the config-surface fix live?** Options: (a) a new dedicated work item (`discovered-from:SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91`, owner Build); (b) extend `SA-0MUILGH5E007X627`'s ACs. **Recommended: (a)** — `SA-0MUILGH5E007X627` explicitly requires config rewrites to remain detected, so folding this in would contradict its current ACs.
- **OPEN QUESTION Q3 — Guard exclusion scope.** Options: (a) exclude only `branch.<ref>.{remote,merge}` keys for refs in `excluded_refs` (derived from `git worktree list --porcelain`); (b) exclude all `branch.wl-*` config (rejected: name patterns destroy detection); (c) exclude the whole config surface (rejected: weakens genuine mutation detection). **Recommended: (a)**.
